caption:
The silence of the library at 8 PM is the best kind of invitation... 🤫

There’s something intoxicating about the way the dust motes dance in the golden glow of the desk lamp, casting long shadows over the ancient leather-bound books. I know I should be grading papers, but the way my student looks at me across the heavy oak table makes it impossible to focus on anything but the tension thickening between us. It's a dangerous game, one where the rules of the classroom feel miles away.

I’m wearing my favorite silk-blend dress—the one that feels like a secret against my skin. It’s professional enough for a lecture, but as I lean forward to point out a specific passage in our text, the fabric pulls just enough to highlight every curve. I can feel his eyes trace the line of my neck before settling on the way my blouse buttons strain slightly. It’s a silent conversation, a heavy, magnetic pull that makes the air feel thick.

"This chapter is... complicated," I whisper, my voice barely audible over the steady ticking of the grandfather clock in the corner. I move a bit closer, the scent of old paper and my perfume mixing in the air. I can see his breath hitch. My heart is racing, a rhythmic thrum against my ribs that I’m sure he can see in my eyes. 

We’re supposed to be discussing 18th-century poetry, but we’re actually exploring something far more primal. The proximity is electric. I let my hand linger a second too long on the page, my fingers brushing against his. A small, daring smile plays on my lips. This isn't in the syllabus, but I think it’s the most interesting lesson we’ve had all semester. 🖋️✨
